mapping.Rationale: AMLO has no alert concept; defined in the Investigation Ontology (Demo)
mapping.Why (plain): The AML ontology has no concept of an alert, so the Investigation ontology adds one.

mapping.Rationale: Identifier from the monitoring system
mapping.Why (plain): The alert's own reference number, kept as it comes from the monitoring system.

mapping.Rationale: ISO-8601 string coerced to xsd:dateTime by the context; source timestamps must be normalised to UTC before this step
mapping.Why (plain): Stored as a real date and time, so alerts can be sorted and compared by time. Times should be in UTC first.

mapping.Rationale: Free text from the monitoring system; deliberately not mapped to a technique automatically (rule-to-technique mapping is a separate table that needs expert review)
mapping.Why (plain): The monitoring system's own explanation, kept as text. It is not turned into a technique automatically: matching rules to techniques needs an expert to review it.

mapping.Rationale: The id string is prefixed into an AML typology IRI in adapters.py. A technique is an individual of amlo:Technique so it is referenced as a value and never used as @type. It is a hypothesis
mapping.Why (plain): The monitoring system gives only a technique code. Turning it into a pointer to the AML typology technique lets the agent pull in that technique's indicators. It is a hypothesis to check, not a conclusion.

mapping.Rationale: AMLO has no evidence concept
mapping.Why (plain): The AML ontology has no concept of evidence, so the Investigation ontology adds one.

mapping.Rationale: Points to an AML typology data source. A data source is a TYPE of record (for example Transaction Logs); the evidence item is the instance
mapping.Why (plain): Says what kind of record the evidence is, for example a transaction log. It points to that kind of record in AML typology, not to this one record.

mapping.Rationale: One indicator to check for this alert
mapping.Why (plain): One thing to check for this alert, tied to one risk indicator.

mapping.Rationale: AML typology indicator individual used as is
mapping.Why (plain): A risk indicator taken straight from AML typology, unchanged.

mapping.Rationale: Whole number from 1 upwards (SHACL); 1 is first
mapping.Why (plain): The order to look in: 1 is first. It must be a whole number from 1 upwards.

mapping.Rationale: The adviser's reasoning for this alert. Advice only: nothing is queried or confirmed
mapping.Why (plain): The agent's reason for suggesting this check on this alert. It is advice only: nothing has been looked up or confirmed.

mapping.Rationale: Points to an AML typology data source (a type of record). validate.py checks that AML typology lists it for the suspected technique
mapping.Why (plain): Where to look, as a pointer to a kind of record in AML typology. Code checks that AML typology lists it for the suspected technique.

mapping.Rationale: AMLO has no case concept
mapping.Why (plain): The AML ontology has no concept of a case, so the Investigation ontology adds one.

mapping.Rationale: Same treatment as the suspected technique of an alert
mapping.Why (plain): The technique the investigator is testing. Like an alert's suspected technique, it is a pointer to AML typology and a hypothesis, not a conclusion.

mapping.Rationale: One assessment of one indicator
mapping.Why (plain): One investigator judgement about one indicator.

mapping.Rationale: AML typology individuals used as values
mapping.Why (plain): The technique and indicator being judged, taken straight from AML typology.

mapping.Rationale: Four values enforced by SHACL: supported, not-supported, inconclusive, not-assessable
mapping.Why (plain): The judgement on the indicator. Only four values are allowed: supported, not supported, inconclusive, not assessable.

mapping.Rationale: Investigator's wording
mapping.Why (plain): What the investigator saw, in their own words.

mapping.Rationale: Required when status is supported (SHACL)
mapping.Why (plain): The evidence behind the finding. Required when the finding is marked supported.

mapping.Rationale: A draft only; review_status says it needs an investigator
mapping.Why (plain): A draft only. Its review status shows that an investigator still has to review it.

mapping.Rationale: Order matters in a narrative so an RDF list is used
mapping.Why (plain): Kept as an ordered list, because the order of paragraphs matters in a narrative.

mapping.Rationale: Every paragraph must rest on at least one finding
mapping.Why (plain): Every paragraph must rest on at least one finding.

mapping.Rationale: AMLO has no party, account or transaction concepts. AML typology Actor and ProductService are role and product TYPES, not individuals. Out of scope for this demo
mapping.Why (plain): The AML ontology has no party, account or transaction concepts. AML typology's Actor and Product/Service are kinds of roles and products, not individual people or accounts. Left out of this demo.

mapping.Rationale: AML typology M0018 is a mitigation (a control) and not a report event; mapping a filing to it would confuse a control with an event
mapping.Why (plain): The closest AML typology item is a mitigation, which is a control, not a reporting event. Mapping a filing to it would confuse a control with an event.

s3.records: Scenario 3 has no record to map field by field: the agent writes a query. What the integration layer gives it is the data dictionary. For each column it states the type and what the column means in words, so that the words of a risk indicator can be tied to columns. The table is also tied to one AML typology data source, a draft by people; the other data sources AML typology lists for the technique are not in this database, so indicators that need them cannot be shown.
s3.checks: Beyond the dictionary, a guard checks the SQL before it runs: one read-only SELECT over the listed columns only (the laundering label and the round-trip flag are not in the view), with a LIMIT, a tx_id column and the time column.

dictionary.description: One row per payment from one account to another. The data is synthetic.

data_source.name: Transaction Logs
data_source.note: The AML typology data source this table stands for. A first draft written by people: of the data sources AML typology lists for a technique, the payments table is the one that holds transaction records.

columns.name: ts
columns.meaning: When the payment was made, to the minute.

columns.name: from_account
columns.meaning: The account the money leaves. An account id such as 80308DE40.

columns.name: to_account
columns.meaning: The account the money arrives in.

columns.name: amount_log
columns.meaning: ln(1 + amount paid). This is a natural logarithm, NOT the amount: an amount of 1000 is stored as about 6.9. Compare amounts with each other through this column, or avoid comparing amounts.

columns.name: is_cross_currency
columns.meaning: True when the payment currency differs from the receiving currency.

columns.name: is_self_transfer
columns.meaning: True when from_account and to_account are the same account.

columns.name: is_same_bank
columns.meaning: True when both accounts are at the same bank.

columns.name: fmt_wire
columns.meaning: 1 when the payment format is a wire transfer, else 0.

columns.name: fmt_ach
columns.meaning: 1 when the payment format is ACH, else 0.

columns.name: fmt_cheque
columns.meaning: 1 when the payment format is a cheque, else 0.

columns.name: fmt_cash
columns.meaning: 1 when the payment format is cash, else 0.

columns.name: fmt_credit_card
columns.meaning: 1 when the payment format is a credit card, else 0.

columns.name: fmt_bitcoin
columns.meaning: 1 when the payment format is bitcoin, else 0.

columns.name: fmt_reinvestment
columns.meaning: 1 when the payment format is a reinvestment, else 0.
